fixed.item: breakages.json row (outdoor_plants, G7): the P1 gate's substep cost 3.85 ms vs ADOPT 3.21; this domain's share +0.19 ms (weather 0.03 -> 0.09, weather_slow, patio, garden, yard, pool).
fixed.how: Root causes measured with a per-call timer of the bench loop (first vs later calls) and profiles: (1) the kernel's step-start read views (review M3) made each first static-index build inside a substep about three times dearer (0.2-0.45 ms per index on a 929-entity house; a plain build is about 0.1 ms) and this domain built ~20 indexes in the first slow tick of every episode, own_drying's predicate (25 is_type calls per record) costing 3.7 ms alone: garden/patio/pool/yard/weather_slow first calls 0.6-4.7 ms each, which is why systems whose code did not change doubled against ADOPT; (2) the deferred wind copy (phase-1 change) ran kenv.exposed (hooks), floor_cell, footprints, door_clearance and a rest-cell probe for every loose outdoor thing on every substep with gusts of 6 m/s or more (2 of the 4 bench seeds) before kenv.wind_effect's own cheap bound said none of them moves, built the outdoor children map up front and a set of all ~580 wind candidates in the house every substep. Fixes (exact, nothing computed changes): common.py gets index_reads / episode_index / episode_types and an episode_start hook prebuild_indexes (order -70: after safety's, tools_vehicles', mechanisms' and pets' prebuilds at -100..-80, which write nothing, before any hook writes) that builds every index the systems, idle probes and invariants look up in an episode on the plain records (declared reads; the World's no-journal fast path) -- 13 named indexes (windows, lights, grow_lights, thermal_sources, emitters, irrigation_controllers, fire_holders, propane_tanks, pool_chemicals, garden_chemicals, paved_surfaces, slow_weather, wind_loose [outdoor houses only]) and 19 type lists; type_index and static_ids pass declared reads; every lambda predicate became a named one with declared reads; own_drying is two frozenset tests; weather_slow walks one index (slow_weather = own-drying types or surfaces; it was the union of two). weather.wind_effects: a type pre-filter decides the common no-kind case without the is_type chain, the wind candidates are bisected in the sorted static index (no per-substep set), the children map is built just before the pass's first possible write (so it is the pass-start map, as before), and _object_wind checks kernel_cannot_move -- the kernel's private environment._cannot_move term for term, pinned to it -- before exposure/footprint/clearance work (wind_effect returns at that same bound without a write). The unused wind_vector call was dropped.

Publish phys.environment._cannot_move(rec, v, gust) and _free_to_move(state, eid) as cannot_move / free_to_move (the phase-1 request, still open). outdoor_plants.weather.kernel_cannot_move is a term-for-term copy used as the deferred wind copy's first gate (G7); Phase1FinishTests.test_the_wind_pass_gate_is_the_kernels_own_bound pins it to the private function, and the domain switches to the public one once it exists.

World._matching (house_sim/kernel/world.py): when `reads` is declared, evaluate the predicate on the plain record for every entity that has no journal snapshot and no quiet start values this step (its step-start record is the record itself), even when the journal is non-empty; only journaled entities need _StartView. Exact by construction, and every lazy index build inside a substep gets about 3x cheaper for all domains (measured on seed 2, 929 entities, mid-substep: a 2-field type predicate 0.31 ms through views vs about 0.1 ms on plain records; own_drying's old predicate 3.7 ms). Domains (safety, tools_vehicles, mechanisms, pets, people and now outdoor_plants) work around it by prebuilding at episode start; with the change those prebuilds would be optional.

A phys hook for liquid arriving in a holder a domain models itself (e.g. run_hooks('phys.liquid_arrives', w, eid, liters, liquid, source, by) -> liters taken, asked by liquids.pour_in, _catch and deposit_below before pooling): plant_pot, nursery_pot and seed_tray are kernel holders (holds_liquid True), so a kernel pour, drip or overflow into a pot pools liquid_l that outdoor_plants' soil-water model never reads. Repro: build {dwelling: house, residents: minimal, pets: none} seed 0 with a plant_pot spawned on the living_room floor; liquids.pour_in(w, pot, 0.5, 'water') returns (0.5, 0.0) and leaves liquid_l 0.5 with medium.moisture unchanged. outdoor_plants would answer it by wetting the medium and draining the excess through drainage_hole into the saucer (plants.add_water_to_pot's rule).
